hook: SCP-1812 is an extra moon that nobody can see until someone else points to it. Go in knowing that the containment section is really about controlling who knows, not where the object is, and that its worst effects play out on the coastlines of the people who have been told.
whyItMatters:
The article is a tidy example of a memetic anomaly whose consequences are physical for the believer and nobody else. The water it raises does not exist for outside observers, yet it can still kill the people who perceive it.

The procedures are written as a ladder of escalation tied to how many people are aware, from watching hundreds of observatories to spraying amnestics worldwide and emptying coastlines. Treating an idea as a planetary threat is what earns it the Keter label.
thingsToNotice:
The discovery addendum quietly sets the tone: Montag fell from a college roof while launching a homemade boat into a sea only he could see, but the Foundation got involved because he survived the fall and then died of suffocation, drowning on dry ground. His journal, the record of everything known about the object, is also named as the main way the meme spreads.

The treatment addendum is the cruelest part. Convincing patients the invisible liquid is fake makes them lose the ability to perceive real water, so they die of thirst or drown, and some essential staff now live on permanent IV drips; denying the extra moonlight strips away the sight of every star including the sun. Note also that instruments find only empty space unless an aware person runs them, so the document simply chooses to assume the object exists, even while nuclear strikes against it are on the table.
